content.text:
Based on `git blame` of the exact lines the fix commit (9e871e9f) modifies, I traced the buggy code back through the file's history since `MinimalImportScanner.java` was first created.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 37c90f871d12aef228b701cfa53b8332983a26c7, ae1aab70789c2cf6874bf5a4a5ec98becc170979

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation approach:** I followed the history of `MinimalImportScanner.java` (`git log --follow`), which showed only 4 prior commits: `2709a947` (file created), `37c90f87`, `3eeb6399`, `ae1aab70`. I then ran `git blame` on the pre-fix version of the file (`9e871e9f^`) restricted to the exact lines the fix touches, to see which commit last modified each buggy line.

**(2) What was changed / what introduced it:** The fix rewrites three tightly related pieces of logic inside `shouldTypeBeImported`:

- `Set<String> qualifiedNameTokens = new HashSet<>()` → `LinkedList<String>` (preserves insertion order).
- `if (packParent.getParent() != null)` → adds `&& !((CtPackage) packParent).getSimpleName().equals(CtPackage.TOP_LEVEL_PACKAGE_NAME)`, which prevents the package-hierarchy walk from also collecting the unnamed/root package.
- `for (String token : qualifiedNameTokens) { if (fieldAndMethodsNames.contains(token) || localVariablesOfBlock.contains(token)) return true; }` → checks **only the last token** (`qualifiedNameTokens.getLast()`) instead of matching against *any* token in the (unordered) set.

`git blame` on the pre-fix file shows:
- The `packParent.getParent() != null` check and the "match against every token" loop structure were (re)written by **37c90f871** ("Thu Dec 15" — the commit that added `CtExecutableReference` support and substantially rewrote the field/package-traversal block). This is where the flawed "match ANY token, including unrelated package-name segments" algorithm and the incomplete package-terminator condition take their current shape.
- The specific condition body `fieldAndMethodsNames.contains(token) || localVariablesOfBlock.contains(token)` was introduced by **ae1aab70** ("Mon Dec 19"), which split the previous `namedElements` set into `fieldAndMethodsNames` (fields **and method names**, accumulated across the whole compilation-unit scan) and `localVariablesOfBlock`. Because `fieldAndMethodsNames` is a scanner-wide field that is never reset, method names encountered anywhere in the class (e.g. `digest`, matching the package segment `...testclasses.digest`) leak into later, unrelated comparisons.

**(3) Supporting evidence:** The regression test added alongside the fix (`testPrivateStaticImportShouldNotBeImportedInSameClass`) uses `DigestUtil` in package `spoon.test.variable.testclasses.digest`, which not only has a field `STREAM_BUFFER_LENGTH` but also a method named `digest` — the same simple name as the last package segment. Because the pre-fix code (a) iterated over *every* token of the qualified name (field/type/package segments) instead of just the outermost one, and (b) accumulated all method names seen anywhere in the class into `fieldAndMethodsNames`, the package token `"digest"` spuriously matched the method name `digest()`, causing `shouldTypeBeImported` to return `true` and an unwanted `import static ...DigestUtil.STREAM_BUFFER_LENGTH;` to be emitted. This exact failure mode only becomes reachable once both (a) `37c90f871`'s "match any token" package-traversal rewrite and (b) `ae1aab70`'s method-name accumulation into `fieldAndMethodsNames` are in place — hence I attribute the bug jointly to those two commits, with `37c90f871` supplying the core matching/traversal flaw and `ae1aab70` supplying the specific data (method names bleeding across scans) that triggers it in this scenario.

**Uncertainty:** The original file-creation commit `2709a947` already contained a structurally similar (but narrower, field-only) version of this same "check any token" pattern and the same incomplete package-parent-null check, so the design flaw's true origin could arguably be traced there too. I did not run the test suite (read-only investigation only), so I cannot 100% confirm the code would already misbehave at `2709a947`/`3eeb6399` in isolation — my conclusion rests on static code/blame analysis rather than executed reproduction.
